title_en: The Country's Oldest Operating Lighthouse Predates the American Revolution and Still Shines on New York Harbor After More Than 260 Years
title_zh: 这个国家最古老的灯塔早在美国独立战争之前就开始运作了，260多年后仍然照耀着纽约港

paragraphs.en: Until the 20th century, the only safe maritime route into New York Harbor zagged between shallow shoals. At one particularly treacherous point, the shipping lane bent around the northern tip of the Sandy Hook peninsula, which the English politician Thomas Pownall described in 1755 as “a neck of low sandy hills covered with cedars and holly, ending in a low sandy point.” After a devastating series of shipwrecks in 1761, New York’s merchants petitioned the Colonial Assembly to build a navigational aid. Using £750 raised in a lottery, the Assembly purchased four acres of land near the tip of the Sandy Hook peninsula in New Jersey, about seven miles south of Coney Island across Lower New York Bay. On June 11, 1764, the fifth lighthouse in the Colonies was lit atop a stolid, tapered octagon of whitewashed rubblestone, 103 feet high.
paragraphs.zh: 直到20世纪，进入纽约港的唯一安全海上航线都要在浅滩之间曲折穿行。在一个格外危险的地点，航道绕过桑迪胡克半岛（Sandy Hook）北端。英国政治家托马斯·波纳尔（Thomas Pownall）在1755年将其描述为“一片低矮沙丘，覆盖着雪松和冬青，尽头是低矮的沙尖”。1761年发生一连串毁灭性沉船事故后，纽约商人向殖民地议会请愿，要求修建一座助航设施。议会用抽彩筹得的750英镑，在新泽西州桑迪胡克半岛尖端附近购买了四英亩土地，这里隔着下纽约湾，位于康尼岛以南约七英里处。1764年6月11日，殖民地第五座灯塔在坚固的锥形八角形建筑上点亮，塔身由刷白的毛石砌成，高103英尺。

paragraphs.en: When the Revolutionary War began, 11 years later, rebel troops did their best to dismantle Sandy Hook’s lantern, to keep British ships from navigating into New York Harbor. Their efforts included an April 1776 escapade where, as the New-York Journal reported, a New Jersey troupe trapped a group of British soldiers in “the upper room of the lighthouse, where they were carousing,” by “taking away the lower part of the stairs.” But Sandy Hook soon fell under British control. Several other attacks by revolutionaries all failed to destroy the structure or wrest it from the royalists. The walls, more than six feet thick at the base, were simply too strong.
paragraphs.zh: 11年后独立战争爆发时，叛军部队竭力拆毁桑迪胡克的灯室，以阻止英国船只驶入纽约港。他们的行动包括1776年4月的一次突袭。据《纽约日报》（New-York Journal）报道，一队新泽西人“拆掉了楼梯的下半部分”，把一群英国士兵困在“灯塔的上层房间里，他们正在那里饮酒作乐”。但桑迪胡克很快落入英军控制。革命者的另外几次袭击均未能摧毁该建筑，也未能从保皇派手中夺回它。灯塔基座处的墙壁厚度超过六英尺，实在太过坚固。

paragraphs.en: When the British finally withdrew from their last American strongholds, they blasted and burned to pieces the Boston Light , in 1776, and, in 1779, the Beavertail Light , in Rhode Island, two of the oldest beacons in the Colonies. By the end of the century, two other lighthouses that predated Sandy Hook—in Connecticut and Massachusetts—had succumbed to age, fire and battering seas.
paragraphs.zh: 当英国人最终撤出他们在美国的最后据点时，他们于1776年炸毁并烧毁了波士顿灯塔（Boston Light），又于1779年炸毁并烧毁了罗得岛州的比弗泰尔灯塔（Beavertail Light），这两座都是殖民地最古老的灯塔。到18世纪末，另外两座早于桑迪胡克的灯塔——分别位于康涅狄格州和马萨诸塞州——已因年久、火灾和海浪冲击而损毁。

paragraphs.en: Today, Sandy Hook is the oldest continuously operational lighthouse in the United States. It’s also a remarkably rich emblem for a pivotal moment in American statecraft. Before the 1789 Lighthouse Act, which made the country’s 12 surviving lighthouses national property, “the federal state was merely a state of mind,” writes Allen S. Miller, a longtime intelligence and risk-management analyst and civil servant, who is an expert in this history. Predating the act that formally created the Department of Treasury, and signed the same day as the act creating the Department of War, the Lighthouse Act turned those isolated beacons into a pointillist network of federal infrastructure, unifying a fledgling maritime economy and, in the process, helping invent a durable and coherent United States.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，桑迪胡克是美国持续运营时间最长的灯塔。它也是美国治国史上一个关键时刻的极其丰富的象征。1789年《灯塔法案》将全国幸存的12座灯塔收归国有；长期担任情报与风险管理分析师和公务员、也是这段历史专家的艾伦·S·米勒（Allen S. Miller）写道，在该法案之前，“联邦国家只是一种心态”。《灯塔法案》正式设立财政部，并与设立战争部的法案在同一天签署；它早于前者，把这些孤立的灯塔变成了联邦基础设施的点彩网络，统一了初生的海事经济，并在此过程中帮助塑造了一个持久而连贯的美国。
